config.description: v011's weights with v011's INFERENCE reset actually applied. v011 trained with state_reset=4000 but shipped state_reset=0, because the --export-only path read a top-level checkpoint key that is never written and silently defaulted to 0. Same weights, same training, correct serving regime.
config.hypothesis: v011's +0.0058 (36 sigma) was measured under a TRAIN/SERVE MISMATCH, so its true value is unknown and could be higher or lower. The model was trained to expect its recurrent state to be zeroed every 4,000 rows; the submitted bundle never zeroed it, so every prediction from row 4,000 onward came from a state trajectory the model had never been trained under. Chunked-vs-row-by-row parity was 1.466 with the defect and 5.4e-06 without it, which is the size of the discrepancy. Two possibilities, and only a measurement distinguishes them: (a) the reset genuinely helps and the corrected model scores near or above 0.679986, meaning the reported gain was partly masked by serving the model wrong; (b) the reset does not matter and the score moves less than the +0.0003 noise floor, meaning the gain came entirely from the soft mask. Either outcome is worth knowing: (a) makes the reset a real lever worth optimising, (b) means v013's control run is the one that explains v011.
config.change_vs_parent:
NO TRAINING CHANGE. Identical weights to v011: same seed 1337, same 3-epoch cosine schedule, same soft mask, same state_reset 4000 in training, same architecture 2x128. The ONLY difference is at export: feature_stats.npz carries state_reset=4000 instead of 0, which is what solution.py reads at inference. This is a bug fix to the serving path, not a new experiment.
WHY A NEW VERSION RATHER THAN FIXING v011 IN PLACE (AGENTS.md section 2.5 immutability): submissions/submission_gru_v011/ was actually uploaded and scored 0.6515. That record must stay intact and auditable -- a defective artifact that was submitted is exactly the kind of thing the immutability rule exists to preserve. v015 supersedes it with the same weights and a correct export.
